title: Phase 10 · Transformers & Attention
outline:
Phase 10 video (Algorithms, ECM3428): 'Transformers & Attention', sub line 'How AI learned to pay attention'. 11 scenes, about 127 s: title (4), words to numbers (13), softmax (11.5), attention (12), query and key (13.5), values (12.5), several heads (13), one layer (13), the decoder (14), beyond text (12), recap (9). Story: a transformer cannot read letters, so text is cut into TOKENS, every token is looked up as a list of numbers (its embedding) and a POSITION pattern is added, otherwise the two copies of a word in 'the bank by the river bank' would get identical numbers (scene 2). Attention needs SOFTMAX, which turns any scores into shares that add up to 1: scores 2, 1, 0 become e^score = 7.39, 2.72, 1.00, total 11.11, shares 0.67, 0.24, 0.09; scores 4, 2, 0 give 0.87 for the top one (scene 3). ATTENTION: to read 'it' in 'The robot moved because it detected danger' the word looks at every word, itself included, gives each a share and rebuilds its meaning from the ones that matter (it leans on robot); every word does it at once, 7 x 7 = 49 shares (scene 4; the scores are illustrative, see below). By hand on 'the dog barked' (scenes 5 and 6): every word makes a query, a key and a value; the query of barked [1, 1] against the keys [1, 0], [1, 2], [1, 1] gives scores 1, 3, 2 (dog matches best), divided by 1.41 (the square root of 2) = 0.71, 2.12, 1.41, softmax = 0.14, 0.58, 0.28; the shares blend the values: 0.14 x [2, 1] + 0.58 x [1, 3] + 0.28 x [1, 1] = [1.14, 2.15] for barked, and doing every word at once is one 3 x 3 grid of shares times the stack of values. MULTI-HEAD (scene 7): four heads run side by side, each with its own query, key and value and its own pattern (who is 'it'?, the word before, who acts?, acts on what?), each hands back 64 / 4 = 16 numbers per word and the four are glued into 4 x 16 = 64. ONE LAYER (scene 8): attention, then a feed-forward network that treats each word alone, each wrapped in Add & Norm (a skip connection x + F(x) and layer norm): x = [1, 3, 5, 7], F(x) = [2, -1, 0.5, -2], x + F(x) = [3, 2, 5.5, 5] (mean 3.875), after layer norm [-0.61, -1.31, 1.14, 0.79] (mean 0); same shape in and out, so identical layers stack (6 in the original paper). THE DECODER (scene 9): it starts from <sos>, gives every possible next word a share, writes the likeliest, appends it and goes round again until <eos>; masked attention lets a word look only at itself and the words before it: 'Ich habe einen Apfel gegessen <eos>' (toy scores; top shares 0.74, 0.52, 0.64, 0.74, 0.71, 0.97; step 3: einen 0.64, eine 0.24, den 0.09, meinen 0.03). BEYOND TEXT (scene 10): a 224 x 224 picture cut into 16 x 16 patches = 14 x 14 = 196 tokens, 196 x 196 = 38,416 scores; 8 x 8 patches = 28 x 28 = 784 tokens (4 times) and 784 x 784 = 614,656 scores (16 times). Not covered (mention nothing about them): the causal mask as minus infinity, cross-attention from the decoder to the encoder, temperature and sampling, encoder-only / decoder-only / encoder-decoder arrangements, audio and spectrograms, the feed-forward sizes 512 and 2048, why the 1.41 matters in depth, the code lab 10.C (the recap points to it) and the course recap 10.9.

LESSONS the facts come from: a10-tokens 10.1, a10-softmax 10.2, a10-attn 10.3, a10-qkv 10.4, a10-heads 10.5, a10-block 10.6, a10-decoder 10.7, a10-uses 10.8, a10-code 10.C; js/content/algo/algo-p10.js, algo-p9-x-03.js (10.1, 10.8), algo-p9-x-11.js (10.2), algo-p9-x-10.js (10.4), algo-p9-x-12.js (10.5), algo-p9-x-02.js (10.6), algo-p9-x-04.js (10.7), algo-workshops-10-01.js, boss-algo-p9-x.js; bank js/bank/algo-*.js.

THE EXAMPLE DATA (all asserted when the page loads by videos/a10/common.js; a wrong number throws an Error). Scene 2: the lesson's 6 tokens and 8-number embeddings (first 4 shown) and its sine / cosine position pattern (first 4 of 8): bank at slot 1 = 0.7 0.5 -0.4 0.3 + 0.8 0.5 0.1 1.0 = 1.5 1.0 -0.3 1.3, bank at slot 5 = 0.7 0.5 -0.4 0.3 + -1.0 0.3 0.5 0.9 = -0.3 0.8 0.1 1.2; without position the distance between the two banks (and the two thes) is 0. Scene 3: lesson 10.2's calculator defaults. Scenes 4 and 7: A10.ATT, the robot sentence with 7 words; the 7 x 7 shares are MADE-UP scores pushed through the real softmax (it -> robot 0.82, itself 0.11, the others 0.01; the four head patterns have shares 0.95 to 0.97 on their strong links, the same recipes as lesson 10.5's playground). They are illustrative: the app's own hand-tuned heatmap in lesson 10.3 gives it -> robot 0.17 (biggest of its row, but gentle), so scene 4 prints no share number and shows the shares only as arc thickness and bar length. Scenes 5 and 6: lesson 10.4's X, W_Q, W_K, W_V for 'the dog barked' (Q = [2,1] [1,2] [1,1], K = [1,0] [1,2] [1,1], V = [2,1] [1,3] [1,1], scores QK^T = [2,4,3] [1,5,3] [1,3,2], A = [0.14 0.58 0.28] [0.05 0.77 0.19] [0.14 0.58 0.28], Z = [1.14 2.15] [1.05 2.54] [1.14 2.15]). Scene 7: d_model 64, 4 heads, d_head 16. Scene 8: lesson 10.6's x and F(x), N = 6. Scene 9: lesson 10.7's toy scores (Ich [4, 2.5, 1.5, 1] ...), a mask of the 7 slots (21 masked, 28 allowed, never printed). Scene 10: lesson 10.8.

VIDEO-WIDE CONVENTIONS. COLOURS (whole video): purple = the QUERY (the word asking, the question being put); blue = the KEYS and the numbers that describe a word (embedding, scores, a vector being worked on); orange = what is ADDED or HANDED OVER (the position pattern, the values, the skip path, a thing being compared); green = the RESULT (shares and weights, a new vector, the model input, the winner); red = BLOCKED or too costly (the masked future, a cost that explodes); grey = words (tokens) and anything neutral. Every digit and label is 28 px or more (the helpers throw otherwise); symbols (plus, times, divide, equals, tick, cross, arrow, question mark) are SVG pictograms (A10.op / A10.qmark / L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow), never glyphs, but a times or divide sign INSIDE a label such as '4 × 16 = 64' or '÷ 1.41' is an ordinary character of the font and is fine. Never dim text with opacity below about 0.8: fade a whole group out instead, or switch a tile to the grey tone. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (update(t) is pure); keep 12 px between the figure and the stage edges (nothing outside x 12..924, y 12..630). const V = window.VID, A10 = V.a10, L5 = V.l5 and const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. x, y in a tag's or cell's set() are OFFSETS from where it was built. Read the API comments at the top of videos/a10/common*.js first: they are the contract. ONE SENTENCE, ONE LOOK: the robot sentence (scenes 4 and 7) is always drawn with A10.sentence at x 16, gap 8, so its words sit at the same x in both scenes; 'the dog barked' (scenes 5, 6, 8) is a different, tiny sentence. SHARED PICTURES: a vector is always a stack or row of small cells (A10.cells), a word is a grey tag, a share is a green tag or cell, an arc is one word looking at another (scenes 4, 7, 9), a grid has rows = the word looking and columns = the word looked at (scenes 6 and 9). Words used on screen: 'token', 'query', 'key', 'value', 'share', 'head', 'layer', 'masked'; 'embedding' and 'transformer' never appear in a caption; 'softmax' is named by the headline of scene 3 and reused in the last caption of scene 5; 'attention' and 'Add & Norm' appear as labels. title: Words become numbers,
plus their position
caps: Text is cut into tokens.
Each token becomes a list of numbers.
The two banks get exactly the same numbers.
Nothing says which one came first.
Add a position pattern to every token.
Now the two banks are different.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: a computer cannot read words, so text is cut into TOKENS (here whole words) and every token is looked up in a table that gives it a list of numbers (its embedding, learned in training). The same word always gets the same list, wherever it sits, so on its own the model could not tell which word came first (lesson 10.1). The cure: add a POSITION PATTERN (sines and cosines of the slot number, one list of numbers per slot) to each token's numbers; after the addition two copies of the same word have different numbers. Sentence of lesson 10.1: 'the bank by the river bank'; the video shows the first 4 of the lesson's 8 numbers per token. title: Softmax turns scores
into shares
caps: Imagine three words, each with a score.
Stretch the scores: the biggest grows most.
Divide by the total: the shares add to 1.

title: Every word looks at
every other word
caps: Which noun does “it” stand for?
It looks at every word in the sentence.
But some words matter more than others.
Its new meaning leans on “robot”.
Every word does this, all at the same time.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: ATTENTION. Each head hands back a short list for every word (16 numbers when the model width is 64 and there are 4 heads: 64 / 4 = 16); the four short lists are glued side by side (concatenated) into 64 numbers (4 x 16 = 64). title: Each layer mixes words,
then thinks about each
caps: A layer has two main parts.
Attention lets the words share information.
A skip path adds the input back.
Norm keeps the numbers steady.
The network then treats each word alone.
Same shape in and out, so layers stack.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: ONE LAYER of the transformer (lesson 10.6): attention first (the words exchange information), then a small feed-forward network that works on each word alone; each part is wrapped in 'Add & Norm': a SKIP connection adds the input back (x + F(x): if the part adds nothing, x passes through unchanged) and a layer norm re-centres and rescales each word's numbers (mean 0, spread 1). title: The decoder writes
one word at a time
caps: Writing starts from a start token.
Every possible next word gets a share.

scenes.spec:
IDEA: the DECODER writes a sentence one word at a time (lesson 10.7), here the German translation of 'I have eaten an apple' with toy scores. title: Anything can be cut
into tokens
caps: A picture can be cut into patches.
Each patch is a token: 196 in all.
Every token scores every token: 196 × 196.
Half-size patches: four times the tokens.

scenes.spec:
IDEA: anything that can be cut into tokens can go through a transformer, not only words: a Vision Transformer cuts a picture into square PATCHES and treats each patch as a token (lesson 10.8). Every file starts with a long API comment listing every signature, option and return value: READ THEM FIRST, they are the contract. Every set() / update() is pure: call it each frame from update(t) with everything you want to see; nothing is remembered between frames; no Math.random, Date or timers.

FLAT PIECES (common-2.js): A10.tag(parent, {x, y, text, tone, solid, ghost, fs, w, h}).set({text, tone, solid, ghost, k, x, y, s, r, o}) with mid() / top() / bottom() / left() / right() (x, y in set() are OFFSETS; k 0..1 pops it in; ghost = dashed empty slot), A10.tagW(text) / textW (exact Nunito 900 widths: a 28 px tag is text + 42), A10.cells(parent, {x, y, texts, w, h, gap, dir: 'row' | 'col', tone, tones, solid, radius}).set(i, {text, tone, solid, ghost, x, y, s, sx, r, o, ring, ringK, ringDash}) with flip(i, k, {from, to, tone, toTone, hop}), all(fn), mid(i) / top(i) ..., A10.disc(parent, {x, y, size, text, tone}) (x, y = CENTRE; 1-2 characters), A10.card(parent, {x, y, w, h, text, tone, plain}), icons A10.op('plus' | 'minus' | 'times' | 'div' | 'equals', x, y, size, tone) and A10.qmark(x, y, size, tone) (append them to A10.svg(parent), then V.place the g), A10.svg (= L5.svg), L5.tick / cross / arrow / drawOn, timing A10.seq(t, t0, step, dur, i) and A10.pop(k) -> {s, o}. NOTES FOR SCENE AUTHORS. (1) x, y in a tag's or cell's set() are OFFSETS from where it was built; A10.arc and the icons use ABSOLUTE stage coordinates. (2) Create every handle in build(); A10.svg creates a full-stage svg, so create it before the tags that must sit on top of the arcs. (3) A group that must fade as a whole (a beat of scene 6 or 8) is a wrapper div (position absolute, left 0, top 0): pass it as the parent of everything in the beat and V.place(wrapper, {o}). (4) To dim something, switch its tone to grey or fade a whole group; never lower the opacity of text below about 0.8. (5) Every number you print comes from A10; assert the ones the storyboard names with A10.same / A10.close. (6) No text under 28 px, nothing outside x 12..924 or y 12..630 of the stage, never white, no gradients. (7) Scene 4 prints NO share number (the shares are illustrative, see the outline). (8) The recap keeps every pictogram inside x 0..320 of its 340 px box.
